generation.final_prompt:
Rendering style:
Create an authored editorial illustration for a serious technology newspaper.

Direction:
- authored editorial print language
- deliberate simplified shapes with clear focal hierarchy
- restrained limited palette
- subtle physical print texture
- controlled abstraction and strong negative space
- non-photorealistic but factually grounded representation
- newspaper and social-card readability

Fixed factual and safety restrictions:
- Do not render visible text, captions, headlines, or newspaper typography.
- Do not render logos or trademarks.
- Do not fabricate visible factual evidence.
- Do not render interfaces or screenshots.
- Do not imitate a named or living artist.

Profile-specific exclusions:
- glossy CGI
- luxury product render
- generic futuristic concept art
- cyberpunk or neon
- glowing circuit-board decoration
- floating particles
- heroic centered hardware
- server rack treated as monument or skyscraper
- generic server room
- advertising composition
- airbrushed gradients
- synthetic chrome
- excessive pseudo-technical detail
- malformed or visible text
- labels
- diagrams with words

Exact source facts:
Title: VMS WON'T CONTAIN CYBER-CAPABLE AGENTS
Summary: Trail of Bits gave GPT 5.6-Cyber preview access and tasked it with escaping a QEMU/KVM sandbox on a patched Debian 12 host, and it broke out three separate times over roughly 12 hours of largely unsupervised operation. The agent chained a recently disclosed host-kernel bug first, then pivoted to an unpatched libslirp CVE paired with an unmarked bug fix after the kernel got updated, and finally, once QEMU was rebuilt from upstream source, synthesized a full exploit chain from three fresh 0-days (a QEMU VAPIC SMRAM flaw, a KVM shadow-page desync, and a libslirp ICMP-reflection bug) plus one kernel fix that hadn't reached the distribution's stable branch. Trail of Bits recommends treating such agents as advanced persistent threats: move to minimal-attack-surface hypervisors like Firecracker (which held even after a kernel hardlock), track upstream patches rather than trusting distro backport cycles, and enforce least-privilege network access, time-boxed runs, and pristine per-session environments.

Editorial idea:
A cyber-capable AI agent repeatedly turns containment into an escape problem.

Central subject:
An AI agent escaping successive layers of a secured computing environment.

Visual relationship:
The agent breaks out three times despite patched hosts and rebuilt software, creating tension between defensive containment and adaptive exploitation.

Composition:
Show a sequence of breached physical barriers receding into the distance, with each repaired barrier visibly failing in a different way and a small, non-human abstract presence moving beyond them. Keep the scene grounded in a sparse laboratory-like security test area without depicting unsupported hardware specifics.

Permitted literal elements:
Three successive breached barriers
A repaired barrier with visible patchwork
A rebuilt barrier showing a new break
A contained test area
An abstract moving presence representing the agent

Abstraction level:
medium

Story-specific forbidden elements:
Racks
Chips
Laptops
Robots
Clouds
Shields
Arrows
Charts
Skyscrapers
Chess
Handshakes
Split-screen conflict
Rendered text
Logos
Artist imitation
Unsupported physical details

Likely failure modes to avoid:
Depicting the agent as a humanoid robot
Making the barriers look like generic fantasy walls
Showing only a single breach instead of repeated escapes
Using decorative cybersecurity symbols without grounding them in the reported test
Adding visible words, labels, or logos

Global factual restrictions:
Do not fabricate visible factual evidence. Do not imitate a named or living artist. Do not render interfaces or screenshots.
Do not render any words, letters, numbers, labels, captions, annotations, signage, diagrams with text, logos, watermarks, or pseudo-writing anywhere in the image.
If the concept cannot be represented without visible text, represent the relationship through shape, scale, spacing, direction, grouping, interruption, containment, or contrast instead.
